subsystems.name: Access shaft
subsystems.role: gets people and cargo from the surface down through the collapsed skylight into the tube.

subsystems.name: Pressure liner
subsystems.role: the actual pressure vessel — a sealed membrane that holds breathable atmosphere inside the tube.
parts: anchoring plates bolted to the floor

subsystems.name: Rock stabilization
subsystems.role: stops the ceiling from spalling and keeps the natural roof load-bearing.

subsystems.name: Life support
subsystems.role: keeps the enclosed volume habitable for weeks or months at a time.

subsystems.name: Power and lighting
subsystems.role: sunlight never reaches the interior, so all energy must be brought in or generated inside.
parts: fission surface power unit or solar array at the skylight
LED lighting for work and plant growth

subsystems.name: Thermal control
subsystems.role: the rock mass is a huge, near-constant-temperature sink that must be managed rather than ignored.
parts: radiators or heat-rejection loop to the surface

buildSteps.title: Find and vet a tube
buildSteps.detail: Orbital imagery and radar locate skylights; ground-penetrating radar and gravity data estimate tube width, ceiling thickness and how close it is to collapse.

buildSteps.title: Send in a robot first
buildSteps.detail: A rappelling or flying probe descends the skylight to map the interior, sample the rock and confirm the roof is sound before anything expensive goes down.

buildSteps.title: Clear and level the floor
buildSteps.detail: Robotic excavators remove rubble and brecciated fall material, then grade and compact a flat pad sized for the habitat footprint.

buildSteps.title: Reinforce the ceiling
buildSteps.detail: Rock bolts and anchors are drilled into the roof, and a sealant or sintered regolith skin is applied to stop loose fragments falling onto the liner.

buildSteps.title: Cast a foundation
buildSteps.detail: A floor slab is built by sintering or 3D-printing local regolith — or by pouring a pressurised concrete-like mix — with anchor points cast in.

buildSteps.title: Install the liner
buildSteps.detail: An inflatable multi-layer membrane is carried down, laid out, and inflated against the tube walls and floor, then tensioned with webbing anchored to the slab.

buildSteps.title: Seal and pressurise
buildSteps.detail: Airlocks are fitted at the shaft, and the volume is slowly pressurised with inert gas while leak-rate and deformation are measured over days.

buildSteps.title: Fit out and commission
buildSteps.detail: Life support, power, lighting and thermal loops are installed and run through a full crewed simulation before the habitat is declared operational.

prerequisites.tech: Orbital and subsurface surveying (radar, imagery, gravity)
prerequisites.why: we can only see skylights from orbit; the tubes themselves are still inferred rather than mapped.
inflatable modules have flown on the ISS, but none has been anchored into rock or operated in reduced gravity with abrasive dust.
bags, sintered bricks and printed structures have been demonstrated on Earth and on orbit, not yet on a planetary surface.
a small reactor design was ground-tested in 2018, but no unit has operated on the Moon or Mars.
recycling rates on the ISS still need to improve before a settlement can go months between resupply.

pathway.milestone: orbital images have identified candidate skylights on the Moon and Mars
pathway.unlocks: a shortlist of sites worth visiting.

pathway.milestone: a robotic probe descends into a skylight and maps the tube
pathway.unlocks: real numbers on tube size, ceiling thickness and collapse risk.

pathway.milestone: a small sealed section is pressurised and held inside a tube
pathway.unlocks: proof that natural rock plus a liner can work as a pressure vessel.

pathway.milestone: a crewed subsurface habitat occupied through a full lunar night
pathway.unlocks: routine shielded living, with surface work as day trips.

pathway.milestone: multi-chamber settlements filling kilometres of tube
pathway.unlocks: large populations off-Earth without importing heavy shielding from Earth.
